title: 4-Week HIIT Workout Plan for Fat Loss
description: High-intensity interval training burns 25-30% more calories than steady-state cardio. This 4-week HIIT plan progressively increases intensity for maximum fat loss.
author: Jake Reynolds

content.text: HIIT (High-Intensity Interval Training) alternates between maximum-effort bursts and active rest. This creates an 'afterburn effect' (EPOC) where your body continues burning calories at an elevated rate for 14–72 hours after exercise.

items: Week 1: 20 seconds on / 40 seconds rest, 15 minutes, 3x/week
Week 2: 25 seconds on / 35 seconds rest, 18 minutes, 3x/week
Week 3: 30 seconds on / 30 seconds rest, 20 minutes, 4x/week
Week 4: 40 seconds on / 20 seconds rest, 25 minutes, 4x/week

content.text: Do not do HIIT more than 4 days per week. Unlike steady-state cardio, HIIT is very taxing on the central nervous system. Overtraining leads to injury and hormonal disruption.

items.question: Is HIIT better than steady-state cardio for fat loss?
items.answer: HIIT burns more calories per minute and creates significant EPOC (afterburn). However, both work. HIIT is more time-efficient, while steady-state cardio is lower impact and easier to recover from. Combining both in a weekly routine is optimal.

items.question: Can I do HIIT every day?
items.answer: No. HIIT requires 48–72 hours of recovery between sessions. Doing it daily leads to overtraining, increased cortisol (which promotes fat storage), injury risk, and performance decline.
